basis: Intellectual disability defines the syndrome; skeletal abnormalities and congenital heart malformations each occur in 30-79%; renal and intestinal anomalies are occasional.
Human disease is chiefly rhinosporidiosis, with persistent nasal or nasopharyngeal granulomatous lesions in most patients (~70-90%).
Inherited lipid metabolic disorder; no additional organ damage is shared by most patients across this broad group.
Malignant neoplasm of cutaneous vascular endothelium, directly occupying skin and its blood vessels; metastatic sites are not intrinsic labels.
TULP1-associated retinal degeneration causes rod-cone dysfunction and visual loss; associated cataracts remain within the ocular axis.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability; no additional organ involvement is established.
GPI biosynthesis defect with encephalopathy; oral overgrowth 75-100%, skeletal abnormalities 50-75%; hearing impairment 33% omitted at cap; hepatomegaly alone insufficient.
MHC II antigen-presentation immunodeficiency; recurrent infections are separate diseases; sparse CNS findings do not establish common direct neurologic injury.
Metaphyseal skeletal dysplasia with short bones and stature; this subtype lacks evidence of common hair abnormalities or immunodeficiency.
Primary ovarian carcinoma; pulmonary type describes morphology rather than lung origin, and neuroendocrine differentiation does not establish endocrine disease.
Bacterial infection defined by organism family; no single anatomical site is established as common across the group.
Benign brown adipose tissue tumor, usually arising in subcutaneous soft tissue; intramuscular and CNS locations are minority presentations.
Benign tumor confined to the endometrium, a reproductive tissue outside the specified axes.
Retinal malignancy with extraocular extension; the definition does not establish any particular distant organ as involved in at least 30%.
Congenital Candida infection commonly produces direct cutaneous infection in most presentations; this is an infected skin eruption, not a nonspecific rash.
Venous malformation with defining fibro-adipose infiltration of skeletal muscle, causing contractures, deformity and atrophy; skin is usually unaffected.
Rickettsial infection; myocarditis and neurologic complications are not common defining manifestations, and fever alone adds no organ axis.
Recurrent ulceration directly affects oral mucosa; an autoimmune or specific immune-mediated disease is not established by the supplied definition.
Carcinoma arises in breast parenchyma; squamous differentiation and pseudoangiosarcomatous morphology do not establish skin or vascular origin.
Isolated congenital underdevelopment of the tongue, an oral structure within the gastrointestinal axis.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss; no additional organ disease is established.
TRPV3-associated mutilating keratoderma with periorificial plaques; corneal disease occurs in 5-29% and digit autoamputation in 1/6, below threshold.
Primary neuroblastoma arising in the cerebral hemispheres.
UNG-related antibody class-switch immunodeficiency; respiratory infections reported in 1/3 are separate infections, not direct intrinsic lung disease.
Peripheral arterial insufficiency causes exertional claudication; reversible muscle pain and weakness do not establish structural skeletal muscle damage.
